definition: The challenge and set of techniques for successfully transferring behaviors or policies learned in a simulated environment to work reliably in the real world.
details: Sim-to-real transfer is a significant challenge in robotics, since simulations inevitably differ from real-world physics and sensor characteristics in ways that can cause policies trained purely in simulation to fail when deployed on real hardware.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. It is the same loop you use to learn anything: try, miss, correct, try again. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. And that is Sim-to-Real Transfer — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
